findings.source_passage: As if the waves had been fullers, this craft was bleached like the skeleton of a stranded walrus.
findings.why_it_matters: The simile 'as if the waves had been fullers' is the interpretively distinctive image — fulling cloth by beating it, applied to the sea's action on the hull — and gives the description its Melvillean texture; the draft drops it entirely, keeping only the walrus-skeleton.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'as if the waves had been fullers' before the bleached-skeleton clause.

findings.source_passage: to any monomaniac man, the veriest trifles capriciously carry meanings.
findings.source_locator: paragraph 5, after description of the fish darting away
findings.why_it_matters: This is a key interpretive gloss on Ahab's psychology — the word 'monomaniac' is the book's clinical-thematic marker for Ahab, and the sentence directly explains the symbolic weight of the fish-omen scene that precedes Ahab's murmur; without it the scene loses its explanatory anchor.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'to any monomaniac man, the veriest trifles capriciously carry meanings' after the fish-darting description.

findings.source_passage: Round the world! There is much in that sound to inspire proud feelings; but whereto does all that circumnavigation conduct? Only through numberless perils to the very point whence we started, where those that we left behind secure, were all the time before us.
findings.why_it_matters: The draft compresses the closing clause to 'to the very point whence we started,' dropping 'where those that we left behind secure, were all the time before us' — which is the rhetorical and emotional payload of the sentence, the ironic inversion that makes the homecoming meditation melancholy rather than merely geographical.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full clause: '...to the very point whence we started, where those that we left behind secure, were all the time before us.'

findings.source_passage: Were this world an endless plain, and by sailing eastward we could for ever reach new distances, and discover sights more sweet and strange than any Cyclades or Islands of King Solomon, then there were promise in the voyage.
findings.why_it_matters: The specific allusions — 'Cyclades or Islands of King Solomon' — are signature Melvillean geographical-mythological phrasing that grounds the philosophical digression in the book's world-spanning imagination; the draft strips them to a generic 'new distances.'
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'discover sights more sweet and strange than any Cyclades or Islands of King Solomon' to preserve the allusive register of the closing meditation.

summary: Four medium-severity failures — the 'fullers' simile erased, the 'monomaniac man' gloss dropped, the homecoming irony truncated, and the Cyclades/Solomon allusions removed — collectively flatten the chapter's voice and strip two interpretively significant passages.
